propositions.text: This appeal arises from Federal Court decision dismissing appellant's judicial review application under Federal Courts Act section 18.1
Federal Court dismissed appellant's mandamus application for failure to identify public legal duty of RCMP Commissioner

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the appeal arises from Federal Court dismissing appellant's judicial review and mandamus applications against RCMP Commissioner.

propositions.text: Federal Court Decision noted appellant's affidavits were disjointed and mixed facts, hearsay, allegations and submissions
Appellant's sister and brother-in-law involved in lengthy Alberta Court divorce and custody proceedings
Appellant's sister made domestic and child abuse allegations against her husband to RCMP

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts facts: appellant's relatives involved in family court, sister made abuse allegations to RCMP, affidavits were disorganized.

propositions.text: In February 2021, appellant filed two complaints to CRCC requesting investigation of RCMP conduct responding to sister's allegations
Under RCMP Act, individuals may complain about RCMP member conduct in performance of duty
CRCC mandate and procedures reviewed in British Columbia Civil Liberties Association v. Canada (RCMP)

paragraphs.summary: The court states appellant filed complaints to CRCC about RCMP conduct; RCMP Act allows complaints; CRCC mandate explained in prior case.

propositions.text: Appellant requested CRCC address management and conduct of Cochrane and Airdrie detachments and senior management failures
CRCC did not address management issue as beyond jurisdiction and referred it to RCMP Commissioner
Allegation referred to RCMP's OISP for internal administrative review

paragraphs.summary: The court notes appellant's request about detachment management was beyond CRCC jurisdiction and referred to RCMP's internal review office.

propositions.text: In April-June 2023, appellant sent emails to Commissioner requesting disclosure of OISP review
May 26 email requested confirmation OISP review would be disclosed in family law proceedings
June 19 email requested response and clarification to 20 questions about OISP review of detachment mismanagement

paragraphs.summary: The court describes appellant's emails to Commissioner requesting disclosure and responses about OISP review and detachment mismanagement.

propositions.text: June 19 email set June 23 deadline for response or appellant would consider RCMP's lack of response a reviewable decision
Appellant alleged RCMP Commissioner made reviewable decision not to address ongoing conduct related to her complaint

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts appellant's June 19 email threatening to treat non-response as reviewable decision alleging RCMP's refusal to address conduct.

propositions.text: Department of Justice responded on behalf of Commissioner seeking clarification of appellant's request and counsel status

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Department of Justice responded seeking clarification and counsel status of appellant.

propositions.text: Appellant filed judicial review application that was heard by Lafrenière J.

paragraphs.summary: The court states appellant filed judicial review application heard by Lafrenière J.

propositions.text: Federal Court judge noted relief sought was narrowed to declaration of breach of RCMP Act duty, order setting aside decision, and mandamus order

paragraphs.summary: The court reports Federal Court judge found relief sought narrowed to breach declaration, setting aside decision, and mandamus order.

propositions.text: Jurisdictional questions under Federal Courts Act s.18.1 assessed on correctness standard
Mandamus public legal duty criterion assessed on correctness; other criteria on palpable and overriding error standard
Standards from Canadian Judicial Council v. Girouard, Air Canada v. Toronto Port Authority, Apotex, and Housen v. Nikolaisen

paragraphs.summary: The court explains jurisdiction and mandamus standards of review and cites relevant authorities.

propositions.text: No error found in Federal Court's reasons

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error in Federal Court's reasons.

propositions.text: A matter not affecting legal rights, obligations, or prejudicial effects is not reviewable
Cites Democracy Watch 2021, Air Canada, Democracy Watch 2009 on reviewability
Commissioner's lack of response to June 19 email was not a reviewable decision
Appellant had no legal right to answers; Commissioner had no legal duty to respond; non-response had no prejudicial effects

paragraphs.summary: The court holds non-response to appellant's email was not reviewable as it did not affect legal rights or duties, citing prior cases.

propositions.text: Same reasoning applies to OISP review; Commissioner had no legal duty to conduct internal review
Results of OISP review do not affect appellant's legal rights

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Commissioner had no legal duty for OISP review and its results do not affect appellant's legal rights.

propositions.text: Appellant argues judicial review is only way to hold RCMP accountable for allegedly misleading Alberta Court

paragraphs.summary: The court states appellant argues judicial review is necessary to hold RCMP accountable for alleged misleading conduct.

propositions.text: Appellant's argument parallels Democracy Watch 2009 where failure to investigate harmed public confidence
Democracy Watch 2009 rejected argument; Ethics Commissioner had no duty beyond statute; refusal to investigate did not affect rights

paragraphs.summary: The court compares appellant's argument to Democracy Watch 2009 where similar claim was rejected for lack of statutory duty.

propositions.text: Parliament creates formal complaints procedures with express duties on public officers
CRCC process does not create general complaints procedure imposing legal obligation beyond statute
Appellant had statutory right to file complaint, have it investigated, and receive response, which she has
Appellant's standing to file complaint was not raised

paragraphs.summary: The court finds CRCC process imposes no legal duty beyond statute; appellant had statutory rights and standing was not challenged.

propositions.text: RCMP delivered report on complaints on January 25, 2024, addressing appellant's 14 allegations in detail
Report concluded investigation concluded and appellant may request CRCC review within 60 days if dissatisfied

paragraphs.summary: The court notes RCMP report concluded investigation and informed appellant of right to request CRCC review if dissatisfied.

propositions.text: Court turns to appellant's request for mandamus order

paragraphs.summary: The court proceeds to consider the mandamus request.

propositions.text: Federal Court found appellant did not meet mandamus test from Apotex requiring public legal duty and clear right

paragraphs.summary: The court reports Federal Court found appellant failed to meet mandamus test requiring public legal duty and clear right.

propositions.text: Appellant cites RCMP Act s.5(1) as source of legal right to have Commissioner respond and investigate misconduct allegations
Appellant contends public legal duty arises from common law police duties described in R. v. Godoy

paragraphs.summary: The court states appellant argues RCMP Act s.5(1) and common law police duties create legal right and public duty to respond and investigate.

propositions.text: These arguments fail.

paragraphs.summary: The court states that these arguments fail.

propositions.text: Subsection 5(1) authorizes the Commissioner to manage and control the RCMP.
Statutory authority to a public official does not create a legal right for citizens to require administrative discretion be exercised in a certain way absent effect on a legal right.
Reisdorf v. Canada, 2023 FCA 188 at para. 8 supports this principle.
No error in Federal Court's finding that Commissioner had no legal obligation to respond within the June 19th email deadline.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains subsection 5(1) authorizes the Commissioner, no legal right arises for citizens to demand discretion be exercised, citing Reisdorf, and finds no error in Federal Court's ruling on the deadline.

propositions.text: The appellant relies on common law duties of the police to support her position.
Common law duties do not impose a positive duty on the Commissioner to respond to the appellant's email.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues common law police duties support her, but the court finds no positive duty to respond arises from them.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed with costs fixed at $2,500.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal with costs of $2,500.
